entry.title: Utah Drops Criminal Charges Against Prediction Platform Kalshi
entry.content:
Links: cnn.com

Utah prosecutors dropped criminal charges against prediction market company Kalshi and its co-founders on Tuesday after the platform voluntarily suspended its operations in the state. The legal move follows a federal court ruling that allowed Utah to enforce its strict anti-gambling laws against the company, prompting the platform's withdrawal from the state's market.

The case highlights a growing regulatory conflict as several states move to classify prediction markets as gambling, while the companies involved argue they should be regulated as financial exchanges under federal law. Kalshi's exit from Utah joins a broader trend of state-level enforcement in Nevada, Michigan, Louisiana, and Washington, with many experts anticipating that the Supreme Court will eventually decide the industry's legal status.

entry.title: On-Chain Analysis Examines Suspected Polymarket Insider Trade Ahead of Jensen Huang NVIDIA Reinstatement
entry.content:
Links: deucalionn.vercel.app | hacker news

An on-chain investigation highlights suspicious trading activity on Polymarket involving a newly created wallet that heavily wagered on Jensen Huang returning as NVIDIA CEO hours before any public announcements. The account accumulated over 71,000 shares at low odds in the middle of the night, just before Donald Trump publicly endorsed Huang's return on social media and NVIDIA officially confirmed his reinstatement.

The transactions were executed in a concentrated burst that absorbed roughly a third of the contract's available sell liquidity using a fresh proxy address with no prior transaction history. While the wallet's anonymity prevents definitive proof of illicit activity, the precise timing and single-market focus illustrate how decentralized prediction markets can expose severe information asymmetries.

entry.title: CrowdStrike Agrees to Acquire Zscaler for $43.9 Billion
entry.content:

CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. has agreed to acquire cybersecurity provider Zscaler Inc. in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $43.9 billion. Under the terms of the agreement, each Zscaler share will convert into 1.135 CrowdStrike shares, representing a roughly 34% premium.

The deal combines CrowdStrike’s Falcon endpoint and cloud security platform with Zscaler's network security and zero-trust capabilities, marking one of the largest acquisitions in the cybersecurity sector. The transaction is expected to close in the second half of CrowdStrike's fiscal 2028, pending regulatory approvals and shareholder votes.
